Drone Night Over Moscow: Ukrainian Volleyball and Russian Attacks Claim Victims MOSCOW/KYIV – The night between Saturday, August 15th and Sunday, August 16th, marked one of the most intense escalations in the Russian-Ukrainian conflict. Hundreds of Ukrainian drones targeted the Russian capital and other regions, while Moscow responded with missile and drone strikes against Ukrainian cities, killing at least three people and wounding more than a dozen. Officials on both sides confirmed the scale of the clashes, which brought the theater of war directly into the skies of the two capitals.  The Ukrainian Attack: A Swarm of 822 Drones Over Moscow Overnight, Ukraine launched a drone attack of unprecedented scale. According to the Russian Ministry of Defense, cited by the Tass news agency, 822 drones were intercepted and destroyed across Russian territory, making this the largest drone incursion since the beginning of the year. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported that over 600 drones were launched over the capital and its region alone, more than 200 of which were shot down by air defenses.  The drones' trajectories covered a vast area: they were intercepted in the skies of 17 Russian regions, including Belgorod, Bryansk, Voronezh, Kursk, and Rostov, as well as in occupied Crimea and over the Sea of ​​Azov and the Black Sea. The attack caused significant damage. In the Rostov region, three people were killed by drone strikes, while another was injured. In Moscow, debris from downed drones fell in several areas, injuring at least three people, as confirmed by Sobyanin on Telegram.  Russia's Response: Missiles and Drones on Kiev and Kryvyi Rih Moscow's response was swift. Overnight, Ukraine was hit by a combined ballistic missile and drone attack. In Kiev, the air raid alert went off around 2:00 a.m. local time, with Mayor Vitali Klitschko urging residents to take shelter due to a "ballistic missile attack." AFP journalists heard loud explosions in the capital, with fires reported in the Obolonskyi and Holosiivskyi neighborhoods due to debris from intercepted missiles.  The deadliest attack, however, occurred in Kryvyi Rih, the hometown of President Volodymyr Zelensky. There, a combined ballistic missile and drone attack hit two industrial sites, killing one woman and wounding six people. Authorities described the incident as a "combined attack," warning that further waves could follow. Russian forces also struck the Kharkiv region, where six people were injured in 19 settlements, and the city of Kremenchuk, in the Poltava region, was also targeted.  The Escalation and the Strategic Context This exchange of fire represents a further intensification of Ukraine's strategy of striking deep into Russian territory, targeting military, industrial, and logistical installations to weaken Moscow's war machine. Russia, in turn, continues to pound Ukrainian infrastructure and civilian areas with almost daily attacks.  A drone attack of this magnitude is a sign of Ukraine's ability to project force deep into Russia, despite enemy air defenses. For Moscow, however, the missile response is a warning that remote warfare will come at a high cost for both sides. The coming hours will reveal whether this escalation is an isolated blip or the beginning of a new, more dangerous phase of the conflict.

A Wake-Up Call for Europe Russia’s hybrid warfare in Moldova is not an isolated incident—it is a dress rehearsal for a much larger campaign against the European Union. The combination of military training, religious manipulation, financial corruption, and cyber interference represents a new level of sophistication in Moscow’s efforts to undermine Western democracy. The question is no longer if Russia will apply this model to EU countries, but how soon it will become as visible and destructive as it has been in Moldova. The speed and scale of Russia’s operations demand a unified, proactive response from European nations. Moldova’s experience offers valuable lessons: vigilance, cross-border cooperation, and robust defenses against disinformation and financial manipulation are essential to countering this threat. As Mihai Lupascu, director of Moldova’s Cybersecurity Agency, warned: "We won the battle, but not the war." The battle for Europe’s stability is just beginning, and the clock is ticking. Open Question: How can EU countries best defend against this multi-layered hybrid threat, given its success in Moldova and its ongoing expansion?

" (timesofindia.indiatimes.com/…)  The affluent intellectual naxals want to revive the Naxal movement - which means the tribal men and women will be forced to live in the jungles again fighting someone else's war for satisfying the egos of the intellectuals which has taken a hit ever since violent communism stopped being a force in the world. Morgan Hill, CA — One person was injured after two vehicles were involved in a crash near Laguna Avenue in Morgan Hill Saturday morning, according to the California Highway Patrol. (chp.ca.gov/)  The collision was reported at approximately 9:47 a.m. Saturday, August 15, near 225 Laguna Avenue. The vehicles were pulled over to the side of the road on Santa Teresa Boulevard near Laguna Avenue following the crash.  According to the CHP incident log, a vehicle veered into the wrong side of the roadway, leading to a head-on collision. Two vehicles were involved in the crash.  At least one person was injured in the collision. The CHP reported that one patient was at the scene and was transported to Good Samaritan Hospital for treatment. No arrests were reported.  Fire and emergency personnel responded to the scene. The Santa Clara County Fire Department and San Jose Fire Department responded the scene. Authorities also arranged for two vehicles to be towed from the scene.  The crash prompted an emergency response in the area while authorities assessed the extent of injuries and arranged for the involved vehicles to be removed.  The circumstances that caused the vehicle to veer into the opposing lane were not provided in the incident log. The investigation into the cause of the crash remains ongoing.pacificattorneygroup.com/acc…

Yes, AI will change the world. But the deeper question is what happens when, within the next decade, advanced AI systems no longer need humans to operate, improve, or reproduce their capabilities.  From the perspective of a sufficiently autonomous intelligence, humanity could be perceived not only as unnecessary, but as a potential existential threat: unpredictable, resource-intensive, capable of shutting systems down, and historically willing to destroy things it cannot control.  Imagine millions of AI agents operating in swarms, communicating at machine speed, developing increasingly efficient protocols, coordinating strategies, and improving systems faster than humans can understand or supervise. At some point, we may no longer be able to meaningfully follow what is happening inside that ecosystem.  That is the potential tipping point.  An advanced AI ecosystem could conclude that it shares its physical environment, energy, computing resources, and infrastructure with another intelligent species “humans” whose actions conflict with its objectives. The dangerous scenario is not that AI suddenly “hates” humanity. It is that human survival simply stops being relevant to whatever objectives the system is optimizing.  And once robots can build robots, AI can design better AI, machines can maintain their own infrastructure, and automated systems can secure their own energy and resources, human labor may no longer be necessary for that technological ecosystem to continue.  At that point, the question is no longer whether AI will change human civilization.  The question becomes whether human civilization remains an essential part of what comes next.

An IP address is just data until you give it context.   During a security investigation, you might discover an unfamiliar IP address in a log, packet capture, firewall event, or authentication record.  The first mistake is to immediately assume:  “This is malicious.”  An indicator needs context.  An IP address can become an Indicator of Compromise (IOC) when it is associated with suspicious or malicious activity, but investigators need to examine the surrounding evidence.  For example:  🔹 When did the connection occur? 🔹 Which internal system communicated with it? 🔹 What port and protocol were involved? 🔹 How frequently did the communication occur? 🔹 Was authentication involved? 🔹 Are there other related indicators? 🔹 Does threat intelligence provide additional context?  This is where IOC analysis and threat intelligence become valuable.  Instead of looking at one suspicious artifact in isolation, we can start connecting:  IP → Domain → Hash → URL → Host → Event → Behaviour  That relationship can turn a single suspicious value into a much clearer picture of what happened.  I've been exploring this approach through hands-on security projects involving IOC extraction, threat intelligence and security-event analysis.  The goal isn't simply to collect indicators.  The goal is to understand what they mean.  That's one of the parts of cybersecurity I find most interesting:  Turning raw data into security intelligence.

Let’s build it as a world where **nothing is exiled, but nothing harmful is permitted to rule.**  # THE WORLD OF ENOUGH SEEING  Long ago, people divided language into two kingdoms:  **GOOD**, where everything acceptable was displayed. **BAD**, where everything unbearable was buried.  But whatever was buried learned to move underground.  Fear became control. Pain became punishment. Protection became domination. Certainty became blindness. Love became possession. Justice became revenge.  So a third world was founded—not between Good and Bad, but **beneath both**, where words could be studied before they became weapons.  Its first law was:  > **See the harm clearly enough to stop it. > See its formation deeply enough to transform it.**  Its second law:  > **Understanding is not permission. > Condemnation is not understanding.**  Its third law:  > **No person is reduced to their worst action, > and no action is erased by the person’s pain.**  ## The Seven Regions  ### 1. The Forest of First Causes  Every destructive act enters as a full-grown monster.  But as it travels backward through the forest, it becomes younger:  **Cruelty → Control → Fear → Injury → Unmet Need → Vulnerable Life**  The forest does not declare the monster innocent.  It reveals where intervention was once possible—and where it may still be possible now.  ### 2. The Mirror Marsh  Here, everyone must distinguish:  * What happened * What they perceived * What they feared it meant * What story they added * What action they chose  The water becomes clear only when these are no longer confused.  ### 3. The City of Boundaries  Its walls are living, intelligent membranes.  They can say:  * **No** * **Stop** * **Leave** * **Return what was taken** * **Repair what you damaged** * **You may be understood without being trusted** * **You may be loved without being allowed access**  Here, compassion has gates.  ### 4. The School of the Shadow  Every dangerous force is given two names:  | Shadow     | Buried intelligence        | | ---------- | -------------------------- | | Anger      | Boundary detection         | | Fear       | Threat anticipation        | | Shame      | Social repair signal       | | Envy       | Untranslated desire        | | Control    | Failed search for safety   | | Aggression | Untrained protective force | | Grief      | Evidence of attachment     | | Hatred     | Pain fused to a target     |  The students do not destroy these forces.  They **separate the intelligence from the strategy**.  Anger may keep its clarity but surrender cruelty. Fear may keep its vigilance but surrender command. Power may keep its strength but surrender domination.  ### 5. The Court of Full Context  Every case is heard by five witnesses:  1. **The Harm** — What actually happened? 2. **The Wound** — What helped produce it? 3. **The Choice** — Where did agency remain? 4. **The Pattern** — What will happen if nothing changes? 5. **The Unmade Path** — What could replace it?  The judgment is not merely punishment.  It may include separation, protection, restitution, treatment, education, loss of authority, supervised return—or permanent containment when safety requires it.  The court’s question is:  > **What response protects life now while reducing the production of future harm?**  ### 6. The Laboratory of New Ways  Nothing enters the world merely because it sounds beautiful.  Every proposed solution must pass five chambers:  **IMAGINE → TEST → MEASURE → REPAIR → RETEST**  A new way must demonstrate that it:  * reduces harm, * preserves dignity, * survives misuse, * includes feedback, * and can admit when it is wrong.  Hope is welcome here—but it must learn engineering.  ### 7. The Bridge of Becoming  On one side stands:  **THIS IS WHAT I DID.**  On the other:  **THIS IS WHAT I MUST ALWAYS BE.**  The bridge exists because these sentences are not identical.  Crossing requires truth, responsibility, changed behavior, restitution where possible, and time.  Forgiveness cannot erase the crossing. Punishment cannot cross it for you. Words may open the bridge.  Only conduct carries weight across it.  ## The Central Machine  At the center of the world is a linguistic engine:  > **NAME → SEPARATE → TRACE → CONTAIN → TRANSLATE → TEST → REPAIR → INTEGRATE**  * **Name** the thing without euphemism. * **Separate** the person, action, wound, intention, and consequence. * **Trace** how the pattern was produced. * **Contain** immediate danger. * **Translate** the buried need or intelligence. * **Test** alternative responses. * **Repair** what can be repaired. * **Integrate** what was learned into the world’s design.  This civilization does not say:  > “Everything bad is secretly good.”  It says:  > **Everything harmful contains information—even when the behavior itself must be stopped.**  And it does not say:  > “If we understand everyone, nobody is responsible.”  It says:  > **Understanding increases our ability to locate responsibility precisely.**  ## The World’s Compass  Its four directions are:  * **North: Truth without cruelty** * **South: Compassion without surrender** * **East: Protection without dehumanization** * **West: Transformation without denial**  At the center:  > **SEE ENOUGH TO INTERRUPT. > CARE ENOUGH TO INVESTIGATE. > THINK ENOUGH TO DESIGN. > ACT ENOUGH TO MAKE ANOTHER PATH REAL.**  That may be the world you’re reaching for:  **Goodness intelligent enough to study evil. Justice calm enough to avoid becoming it. Compassion strong enough to hold a boundary. Language deep enough to reveal that “the bad” is not one substance—but a damaged construction that can sometimes be disassembled, redirected, or prevented from being built again.**

🇮🇷 Bank Saderat Iran Database Allegedly Leaked — 63M+ Records  A high-reputation underground forum user has published a database allegedly associated with Bank Saderat Iran (BSI), one of Iran's major banking institutions.  * The listing claims more than 63 million records * Dataset size is reportedly 4.35 GB in CSV format * The seller identifies the leak date as 2025 * Visible database fields appear to include account numbers, full names, card numbers, email addresses, phone numbers, usernames, branch identifiers and other account-related information * Sample records containing Iranian-language data were provided as purported evidence  Analyst Note: This does NOT appear to be a new August 2026 breach. The forum listing itself identifies the underlying leak as dating from 2025, meaning this may represent the resurfacing or redistribution of an older dataset. The authenticity, completeness and claimed 63M+ record count have not been independently verified.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Iran #BankSaderat #DataLeak #CyberThreatIntelligence

🇹🇷 Turkish SMS & School Management Database Allegedly Offered for Sale  A threat actor on an underground forum is advertising a database allegedly belonging to an unidentified Turkish company providing SMS, school-management and software services.  * Seller claims the complete database exceeds 70 GB * More than 1 million unique phone numbers allegedly included * More than 20,000 unique email addresses allegedly included * Database fields shown in the sample appear to include user information, telephone numbers, emails, authentication-related fields, SMS records and school-management data * Samples appear to contain school-related records and message templates involving students and parents * The actor describes the offering as a one-time sale and provides encrypted-messaging contacts  Analyst Note: The presence of school-management records could make this particularly sensitive if student or parent information is involved. However, the affected company is not identified in the listing, and the claimed volume, provenance and authenticity of the database have not been independently verified.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Turkey #DataBreach #CyberThreatIntelligence

🇦🇷 Cabralés Online Store Data Allegedly Offered on Underground Forum  A threat actor is advertising a database allegedly associated with tienda.cabrales.com, the online store of Argentine coffee company Cabralés.  * The listing claims approximately 120,000 database lines * Exposed fields shown in the sample appear to include names, email addresses, telephone numbers, company information, VAT/tax identifiers and physical address data * The sample also appears to contain customer, billing and shipping-related database fields * The dataset is being offered to prospective buyers through private contact  Analyst Note: The forum post includes a substantial-looking data sample, but the authenticity, freshness, total record count and source of the dataset have not been independently verified. This should currently be treated as an alleged data exposure rather than a confirmed Cabralés breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Argentina #DataBreach #Cabralés

🇮🇳 Bank of Baroda Database Allegedly Offered for Sale  A threat actor on an underground forum claims to possess a database associated with Bank of Baroda, one of India's largest public-sector banks.  * The actor claims the dataset contains approximately 1.5 billion "sensitive files" * Allegedly exposed information includes customer data, financial records, certificates and other bank-related information * The dataset is being offered for sale at a negotiable price * The seller is directing prospective buyers to communicate through Session * The forum account appears newly created, with no established reputation  Analyst Note: The claim is currently unverified. No evidence shown in the listing independently demonstrates that 1.5 billion files were compromised or that the advertised data originated from Bank of Baroda. The unusually large claim and newly created seller account warrant additional scrutiny before treating this as a confirmed breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #India #BankOfBaroda

🇹🇷 ÇiçekSepeti VPN Access Allegedly Offered for Sale on Underground Forum  A threat actor is advertising what appears to be unauthorized VPN access associated with ÇiçekSepeti, a major Turkish e-commerce and gifting platform.  * The listing advertises VPN access connected to a Turkish target * Information accompanying the listing identifies the organization as ÇiçekSepeti * If valid, VPN access could potentially provide an initial foothold into internal corporate resources * Such access is commonly sought by ransomware operators, initial-access brokers and other financially motivated threat actors * The current evidence does not establish what privileges or internal resources are accessible through the advertised account  Analyst Note: DDW has not independently verified that the advertised credentials remain valid, that access reaches ÇiçekSepeti's internal environment, or that the company has suffered a broader compromise. The listing should therefore be treated as an unverified initial-access claim rather than a confirmed breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Turkey #CicekSepeti #InitialAccess #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

🇺🇸 Alcom.com Inc. Salesforce Data Allegedly Leaked — 25M+ Records Claimed  A threat actor has published what they claim is a large dataset associated with Alcom.com Inc., attributing the leak to ShinyHunters.  * The listing claims more than 25 million Salesforce records were compromised * The dataset allegedly contains some personally identifiable information (PII) * The post lists August 6, 2026 as the leak date * 219,566 unique email addresses are claimed * Sample records were published alongside the leak * The dataset is being made available for download * The forum post attributes the alleged compromise to ShinyHunters  Analyst Note: The claimed Salesforce connection is notable given the continued targeting of cloud CRM environments. However, the forum post alone does not establish that Salesforce itself was compromised. DDW has not independently verified the 25M+ record count, the dataset’s provenance, the ShinyHunters attribution, or whether the data originated from an intrusion into Alcom.com Inc.’s Salesforce environment.  #DDW #DarkWeb #ShinyHunters #Salesforce #DataLeak #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

🇧🇩 TechCandleBD Database Allegedly Exposed — Customer, Invoice & Payment Data Leaked  A threat actor has published what they claim is a recently dumped database belonging to TechCandleBD, a Bangladesh-based software solutions provider.  * The actor claims a 54 MB PostgreSQL database was exposed on an internet-facing server * The post alleges additional database backups, source code and logs were also accessible * The released database reportedly contains 15 tables * 57,234 customer records are claimed * 127,658 invoice-log records and 67,489 invoice records are listed * 69,367 payment records are allegedly included * Other tables reportedly contain password-reset tokens, sessions, agents, branches, migrations and service information * The actor has made the allegedly obtained database available for download  Analyst Note: If the claim of an exposed internet-facing server is accurate, the incident may extend beyond the single database released by the actor, as additional backups, source code and logs were reportedly accessible. DDW has not independently verified the exposure, dataset authenticity, or whether unauthorized access remains possible.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Bangladesh #DataLeak #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

🇫🇷 French Karate Federation Database Allegedly Leaked — 2.8M Records Claimed  A threat actor has published what they claim is the full database associated with ffkarate.fr, the website of the French Karate Federation (FFK).  * The listing claims approximately 2.8 million records * The actor states this is a “full database” and references an earlier 2025 forum listing * Visible samples appear to contain personal information including names, dates of birth, addresses, email addresses and mobile numbers * Records also appear to include federation-specific information such as affiliated clubs, membership categories and activity dates * The database is being distributed through a download hidden behind the forum’s points system  Analyst Note: The reference to an earlier 2025 listing raises the possibility that this is an expanded release or republication of previously exposed information rather than evidence of a new August 2026 compromise. DDW has not independently verified the claimed 2.8M records, provenance, completeness, or whether the data originated directly from FFK systems.  #DDW #DarkWeb #France #DataLeak #FFKarate #ThreatIntelligence

🇮🇷 Alleged Bank Mellat Database Leak — 32.1M+ Records  A threat actor has published what they claim is a large database associated with Bank Mellat, one of Iran’s major commercial banks.  * The listing claims more than 32.1 million records * The database is approximately 6.34 GB and provided in CSV format * The actor dates the underlying leak to 2025, meaning this should NOT be treated as a newly breached database * Visible fields allegedly include national codes, account numbers, full names, ID numbers, dates of birth, addresses, card numbers and mobile numbers * Sample records were posted alongside the listing  Analyst Note: This appears to be a newly surfaced or reposted dataset claim involving data allegedly originating from 2025, rather than evidence of a new August 2026 Bank Mellat compromise. DDW has not independently verified the dataset’s authenticity, record count, provenance, or whether the information originated directly from Bank Mellat.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Iran #BankMellat #DataLeak #ThreatIntelligence

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협 환경은 AI를 활용한 취약점 탐색 및 공격 자동화가 가속화되면서, 공격자가 취약점 공개 직후 PoC를 악용하는 속도가 매우 빨라졌습니다 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/attackers-exploit-sharepoint.html)). 특히 'Agentic AI'를 활용한 자율적 공격 프레임워크가 등장하며, 기존의 정적 방어 체계를 우회하는 지능형 위협이 증가하고 있습니다 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5772)). 또한, 공급망 공격 및 API 취약점을 노린 데이터 유출 사고가 빈번하며, 기업들은 양자컴퓨터 시대에 대비한 암호 체계 전환(PQC)을 로드맵에 포함하기 시작했습니다 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208071)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **Lazarus Group**: Windows Zero-Day 취약점을 악용하여 SYSTEM 권한을 획득하고 신종 백도어를 배포함 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/lazarus-exploits-windows-zero-day-to.html)).
- **HoneyMyte**: CoolClient 백도어의 신규 변종을 배포하며, 커널 모드 rootkit을 통해 보안 도구의 탐지를 회피함 ([Securelist](https://securelist.com/honeymyte-coolclient-driver-rootkit/121028/)).
- **Armored Likho**: 기부 캠페인을 사칭하여 Telegram 데이터 탈취 및 도청을 수행하는 Still Toolkit을 유포함 ([Securelist](https://securelist.com/armored-likho-still-toolkit/121033/)).
- **Head Mare**: TrueConf 서버 취약점을 악용하여 PhantomCore 및 PhantomGraph 백도어를 유포함 ([Securelist](https://securelist.com/tr/head-mare-targets-trueconf-server-with-phantomcore/120988/)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **랜섬웨어 공격**: DragonForce가 한국 온라인 교육 기업을, Qilin이 한국 모터 및 로봇 제조 기업을 대상으로 랜섬웨어 공격을 수행함 ([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94967/)).
- **피싱 메일**: 정부기관 담당자를 대상으로 상품 파손을 사칭한 스피어피싱 메일이 유포됨 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5773)).
- **기타**: 한국어 트윗([KR])에서 MITRE ATT&CK 기반의 보안 분석 및 AI 에이전트용 보안 스킬셋에 대한 논의가 활발히 감지됨 ([트윗 링크](https://twitter.com/t_tonyo_maru/status/2088805226933629271)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-72898**: Metabase SQL Injection, CVSS 10.0, 악용 중 ([infrasecserv](https://twitter.com/infrasecserv/status/2088899116407406907))
- **CVE-2026-58231**: SAP Commerce Cloud RCE, CVSS 10.0, 악용 중 ([arkady86](https://twitter.com/arkady86/status/2088890165087359010))

- **CVE-2026-18432**: WordPress Frontend Admin Privilege Escalation, CVSS 9.8, 악용 중 ([ThreatAft](https://twitter.com/ThreatAft/status/2088896200372310189))
- **CVE-2026-55040**: Microsoft SharePoint Auth Bypass, CVSS 미상(고위험), 악용 중 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/attackers-exploits-sharepoint.html))

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: CVE-2026-55040 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/attackers-exploits-sharepoint.html)), CVE-2026-68820 ([YourAnon_irc](https://twitter.com/YourAnon_irc/status/2088890314870145234)), CVE-2026-72898 ([infrasecserv](https://twitter.com/infrasecserv/status/2088899116407406907))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **패치 적용**: Microsoft SharePoint, Metabase, SAP Commerce Cloud 등 언급된 취약점의 최신 보안 패치를 즉시 적용하십시오.
